record.original_question: What are the computational complexities of term-ordering decision problems, including comparability under recursive path ordering with a suitable precedence and lexicographic path ordering with non-total precedences or variables?

evidence.quote: What are the complexities of various term ordering decision problems?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Σ be a finite signature of function symbols, each with a fixed arity, and let V be a countable set of variables. Denote by T(Σ,V) the set of (first-order) terms over Σ and V. A precedence on Σ is a (strict) partial order >_Σ on Σ; it is total if it is a linear order.

Given a precedence >_Σ, the recursive path ordering (RPO) >_rpo on T(Σ,V) is defined as the smallest relation such that s = f(s_1,…,s_m) >_rpo t iff one of the following holds:
 (1) t is a variable occurring strictly in s; or
 (2) t = g(t_1,…,t_n) and either
   (a) s_i ≥_rpo t for some i, or
   (b) f >_Σ g and s >_rpo t_j for all j, or
   (c) f = g and {s_1,…,s_m} is greater than {t_1,…,t_n} in the multiset extension of >_rpo.

The lexicographic path ordering (LPO) >_lpo is defined identically except that case (c) is replaced by the lexicographic extension of >_lpo on the tuples (s_1,…,s_m) and (t_1,…,t_n) (together with s >_lpo t_j for all j).

Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problems:

(i) Given Σ, a precedence >_Σ on Σ (not necessarily total), and two terms s, t ∈ T(Σ,V), decide whether s >_rpo t.

(ii) Given Σ, a (possibly non-total) precedence >_Σ on Σ, and two terms s, t ∈ T(Σ,V) (which may contain variables), decide whether s >_lpo t.

In particular, classify each of these problems with respect to standard complexity classes (P, NP, coNP, PSPACE, etc.), determining tight upper and lower bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known: the constraint satisfaction / orientation problem for RPO is known to be NP-complete, and SAT-based encodings are used in practice; certain first-order theories of RPO (e.g., unary signature, total precedence) are decidable while related LPO theories have undecidability results. However, a complete and tight complexity classification for the comparability problems with non-total precedences and variables was raised as an open question in surveys of rewriting problems, and no comprehensive resolution covering all listed cases is documented in the search results.

status_evidence.title: SAT Solving for Termination Proofs with Recursive Path Orders
status_evidence.snippet: The strict and quasi-RPO decision/constraint problems are decidable and NP-complete; SAT encodings are used in practice.
status_evidence.claim: RPO constraint problems are NP-complete, indicating partial progress on the complexity question.

status_evidence.title: Path ordering (term rewriting) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of RPO/LPO and their decidability/undecidability properties depending on precedence and signature restrictions.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability results differ between RPO and LPO and depend on whether precedence is total.
